alex_sales: Finwise POC saw intermittent 502/503 and occasional TCP RSTs when routing through their firewall + our PrivateLink interface. Happens after a traffic surge during load test.

jamie_se: Can you share the raw error strings? 502 vs 503 vs timeout matters.

alex_sales: Mostly 502/503 from app gateway, some RSTs. Only path via their firewall + our interface endpoint affected; direct test from same AZ to our host OK.

katie_netops: Do they have one interface endpoint in a single AZ and rely on cross-AZ routing? That often causes issues.

alex_sales: They created an interface endpoint in us-west-2a and route other AZstraffic through it.

sam_eng_infra: That's supported but you must watch SNAT and ephemeral ports. If multiple clients are NAT'ed to a small SNAT pool, firewall state can overflow during bursts. Also some providers return AZ-local private IPs for endpoints; inter-AZ traffic may traverse a path their ACLs block.

jamie_se: Does our Private deployment preserve source IPs?

sam_eng_infra: Yes, by default we preserve client source IP on connector/interface endpoint flows. But if customer front-ends NAT everything to a single IP, it looks like thousands of concurrent connections from one IP. Firewall session tables can be exhausted, causing RSTs and 502s.

katie_netops: Ask them to confirm: 1) are they SNATing multiple backend hosts to one external IP; 2) verify ephemeral port range (should be wide, e.g., 1024-65535); 3) ensure ACLs allow ephemeral ports from our endpoint IP range.

alex_sales: They also asked whether VPC peering would avoid the problem.

jamie_se: Peering keeps traffic in VPC routing and may simplify paths, but it won't magically fix SNAT behavior if they still route through a central NAT/proxy. Peering reduces endpoint overlay quirks but you still need per-AZ egress or wide port ranges.

sam_eng_infra: Operational recommendations: - Use one NAT per AZ (distribute source IPs), or - Enable connection reuse/keepalive on app side, - Increase ephemeral port range, - Allow TCP 1024-65535 from our endpoint IPs during POC.

katie_netops: DNS caveat: interface endpoints can resolve to AZ-local IPs. If clients cache a single AZ-local address and then talk cross-AZ, packets can hit unexpected ACLs. Recommend low TTL or our client-side multi-AZ resolution option.

alex_sales: I'll send them a short firewall snippet and trio of actions.

katie_netops: Firewall snippet example to share:

```
# from Finwise firewall
ALLOW TCP 443 from 198.51.100.0/26 -> app-subnet
ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 from 198.51.100.0/26 -> app-subnet
ALLOW TCP 8050,9000 from 198.51.100.0/26 -> health-subnet
```

jamie_se: Pricing note: interface endpoints have per-endpoint-hour + per-GB charges; peering avoids endpoint hour charges but may incur cross-AZ transfer fees. Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable throughput and often lowers per-token cost at scale. We'll include rough numbers in follow-up.

sam_eng_infra: For troubleshooting ask them to run tcpdump on app host and share pcap; check whether RSTs originate from firewall. Example capture:

```
sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host <our-endpoint-ip> and tcp -c 1000 -w /tmp/finwise.pcap
```

alex_sales: Action items I'll send to Finwise: 1) confirm NAT behavior & ephemeral port ranges, 2) open firewall to 1024-65535 for our endpoint IPs for POC, 3) consider per-AZ NAT or VPC peering to reduce central SNAT, 4) run tcpdump/traceroute if issue persists and share captures.

jamie_se: Security questionnaire guidance: PrivateLink gives interface-level isolation and fine-grained security groups, which is good for per-tenant isolation. VPC peering keeps traffic private but shares routing more broadly. Note both keep traffic off the public internet. Offer flow logs and connection traces for audit requests.

katie_netops: Also offer that we can provide ephemeral endpoint IP list and flow log examples for their compliance team during the POC.

alex_sales: Great. I'll send the runbook and ask them to implement port allowlist and check NAT. Will escalate to eng if pcaps show firewall RSTs. :thumbsup:
